recipes.name: PULLED PORK
ingredients: For the Vinegar Based BBQ Sauce
1 tsp 1 Tbsp cayenne pepper (depending on your spice tolerance)
1 tsp 1 Tbsp hot sauce (depending on your spice tolerance)
For the Tomato Based BBQ Sauce
instructions: For the Vinegar Based BBQ Sauce

Combine all the ingredients, whisk together and then transfer to a squeeze bottle for easy distribution. - 1 ½ cups apple cider vinegar - ½ Juice of a lemon - 1 tsp 1 Tbsp cayenne pepper (depending on your spice tolerance) - 1 tsp 1 Tbsp hot sauce (depending on your spice tolerance) - salt - pepper
For the Tomato Based BBQ Sauce

Combine all the ingredients into a pan and cook over medium low heat for 30 minutes, stirring constantly. - 1 cup ketchup - 1 cup brown sugar packed - ½ Juice of a lemon - 3 tbsp butter - 1 tbsp hot sauce - 1 tbsp Worcestershire sauce - ¼ onion grated - 1 tbsp spice rub - ½ cup water
Transfer to a squeeze bottle for easy distribution.
For the Sous Vide Pulled Pork

Combine all spices for dry rub. - ½ cup brown sugar - ½ cup white sugar - ½ cup paprika - 1 tbsp smoked paprika - 1 tbsp dry ground mustard - 1 tbsp garlic powder - 1 tbsp onion powder - 1 ½ tsp ground ginger - 1 tbsp dried oregano - 1 tbsp salt - 1 tbsp pepper

Divide mixture in half. Rub half of mixture evenly all over pork butt, pressing it in until it adheres. Place pork butt in a sous vide–safe vacuum-sealer bag. Add liquid smoke (if using) and seal bag. - 1 in bone Boston pork butt - Homemade dry rub
Set your sous vide to 165°F. When the bath is at temperature, add sealed bag with pork and cover with foil or plastic wrap. Allow to cook for 18 to 24 hours. - For the Pulled Pork

Adjust oven rack to lower-middle position and preheat oven to 300°F. Remove pork from sous vide bag and carefully blot dry with paper towels. (The liquid from the bag can be added to your favorite barbecue sauce and simmered down to provide extra flavor.) Rub reserved spice mixture into the surface of the pork. Place pork on a wire rack set in a rimmed baking sheet and place in oven. Roast until a deep, dark bark has formed, about 1 ½ hours. - Homemade dry rub - For the Pulled Pork - For the Dry Rub

Transfer pork to a large bowl or cutting board. Using a couple of forks, shred meat into bite-size pieces. Place on a bun, top with your BBQ sauce of choice and enjoy! - For the Tomato Based BBQ Sauce - For the Vinegar Based BBQ Sauce
Liberally season your pork with the dry rub. If you have time, wrap in plastic wrap and refrigerate overnight. - 1 in bone Boston pork butt - Homemade dry rub
Place pork into a 250°F smoker. Make sure the fat cap is facing upwards to it bastes the pork while it cooks. Place two small trays of water in the smoker while you cook as well.
Cook for 6-12 hours or until the internal temperature reaches 195°F - 205°F.
Transfer pork to a large bowl or cutting board. Using a couple of forks, shred meat into bite-sized pieces. Place on a bun, top with your BBQ sauce of choice and enjoy!
